name: SRPB
description: In recent years, social robots have gained popularity and many human-aware navigation approaches have emerged. This work presents SRPB – a comprehensive benchmark for the quantitative evaluation of robot navigation methods. It is intended to assist the system designer in selecting the best method for the application. We tested traditional and human-aware trajectory planners with the TIAGo robot in simulated and real-world environments (Fig. 1). We assessed robot behaviour using state-of-the-art task performance scores and novel social metrics regarding robot motion naturalness and the perceived safety of humans surrounding the robot. Our social metrics take human tracking reliability into account. An open-source implementation of our benchmark, compatible with the Robot Operating System, is provided.
evaluation_method: composite_score (safety / comfort / efficiency metrics aggregated) / per-metric rates
general_score_metric: composite_score combining safety incidents, comfort scores, and efficiency (e.g., time-to-goal)
reputation: Academic benchmark from the social-robotics community for evaluating navigation in human-populated environments; used in niche research but not broadly standardized.
notes: Non-LLM robotics benchmark; often small-scale and simulation/controlled-environment focused, so real-world generalization may be limited; metrics can require human judgment for 'comfort'.
